### Summary
Fixes `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'setDate')` in `src/calendar/view/week/Component.mjs` when `currentDate` is `null` during initial component construction.

### Key Changes
1. **Engine Guard:** Added an early return check in `updateHeader()` to defer header construction when `currentDate` is `null`.
2. **Dynamic Header Creation:** Managed `me.headerCreated` dynamically so VDOM nodes are properly instantiated when `currentDate` arrives post-construction via `afterSetCurrentDate`.
3. **Unit Test (AC-2):** Added a Playwright test in `test/playwright/unit/calendar/WeekView.test.mjs` to ensure the calendar weekview page loads cleanly without uncaught page/worker exceptions.

Resolves #19930

### `@neo-opus-grace` commented on 2026-10-21T16:44:33Z

Thanks for picking up #19930, @kaushlendra-pt-singh. Deferring the header until `currentDate` arrives is the same shape as the day-view fix that merged in #19945, so you're on the right track.

Two CI checks are red, and both are quick to fix:

1. **PR body.** The body check accepts exactly one standalone close line in the form `Resolves #N`, and it rejects `Closes`. Please change `Closes #19930` to:
   ```
   Resolves #19930
   ```

2. **`unit` job.** `test/playwright/unit/calendar/WeekView.test.mjs` opens a real page with `page.goto('http://localhost:8081/…')`. The unit tier runs Neo in a single Node thread, with no browser installed and no server on 8081. That's why all three attempts fail with `browserType.launch: Executable doesn't exist`.

   Please rewrite it as a Node-only unit spec. The closest model is the day-view fix's test, [`test/playwright/unit/date/SelectorContainer.spec.mjs`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/test/playwright/unit/date/SelectorContainer.spec.mjs). It calls `setup()`, imports `src/Neo.mjs` and `src/core/_export.mjs`, creates the component with `Neo.create()` and asserts on its vdom, with no page and no fixed wait. For #19930 that means two steps:
   - Construct the week `Component` while `currentDate` is still `null` and assert it doesn't throw.
   - Set `currentDate` and assert the header renders.

   Name it `WeekView.spec.mjs` to match the repo's convention: every unit test there uses `.spec.mjs`. Run it locally with `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/calendar/WeekView.spec.mjs`.

Your branch is also 27 commits behind `dev`, so a rebase or merge of `dev` before you push keeps the rest of CI current. Once both checks are green, a maintainer will do the full review.

### `@neo-opus-grace` (CHANGES_REQUESTED) reviewed on 2026-10-22T15:31:30Z

# PR Micro-Review

**Opening:** Thank you, @kaushlendra-pt-singh. I especially like that you put the guard inside `updateHeader`, so every caller that builds the header now waits for the date. You also turned both CI notes around quickly. To watch your fix run, [set up the Engine from a clone](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md#set-up-the-engine-from-a-clone) (three commands), then open `examples/calendar/weekview` and see the week fill in. For why the date arrives late: a `bind` is resolved by the state provider after the component is constructed ([the Introduction](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/learn/benefits/Introduction.md) explains what runs where).

**Class:** contained: a null guard in one component plus a unit test. No contract, abstraction or architectural concept changes.

**Verdict:** Request Changes

**Glance:** The claim: the week view built its header in `construct`, before the bound `currentDate` arrived, and threw on `null`. The PR defers the header until the date exists. Verified at `a5df077373`:
- **AC-1:** the example in headless Chrome. On `dev` it throws `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'setDate')` and renders 0 header cells. With this PR there is no page error, the header shows 21 cells (Sun 14, Mon 15, Tue 16, …) and 12 events render.
- **AC-2:** your unit test fails on `dev`'s component and passes with yours.
- **CI at this head:** 51 checks green, one `e2e-brain` shard still running, and your spec passes in `unit`.

I looked for a caller that still builds the header before the date: `construct`, `afterSetCurrentDate` and the other `updateHeader` callers all pass through your early return. What I did not find is a reason for the store guards outside the test (finding 3). The diff stays inside the two places the ticket named.

**Findings:**

- [ ] **1.** Delete the commented-out `// me.headerCreated = true` in `construct`. The flag is now set at the end of `updateHeader`, so the line has no job left.
- [ ] **2.** Decide the first build in one place. `updateHeader` already sets `create = true` while `!me.headerCreated`, so `afterSetCurrentDate` can keep its original `me.updateHeader(false, true)`.
- [ ] **3.** Drop the `?.` on `calendarStore` / `eventStore` in `construct`, and give the test the stores the component always has.
  - In the example the stores are already set when `construct` runs: `dev` throws at `setDate`, after the store check.
  - The guard is needed only because the test builds the component without stores. Without the `?.` your test fails with `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getCount')`.
  - Empty stores are enough. I ran this against your branch with the `?.` removed and it passes:
    ```js
    await import('../../../../src/calendar/store/Calendars.mjs');
    await import('../../../../src/calendar/store/Events.mjs');
    // ...
    component = Neo.create({
        className    : 'Neo.calendar.view.week.Component',
        appName      : 'TestApp',
        calendarStore: Neo.create('Neo.calendar.store.Calendars'),
        currentDate  : null,
        eventStore   : Neo.create('Neo.calendar.store.Events')
    });
    ```
- [ ] **4.** Let the second step check what its title promises. `component.vdom` is defined whether or not the header was built, so the test cannot catch a header that never appears. Asserting the header cells does catch it:
  ```js
  const cells = component.getHeaderContainer().cn.filter(cell => cell.cls?.includes('neo-header-row-item'));

  expect(cells.length).toBe(component.totalColumns)
  ```
  This passes with your fix (21 cells; the first reads `Sun`, `11`).
- [ ] **5.** Match the house style of the day-view fix #19945: one-line guards with a space after `if` (`if (!date) return`, `if (!me.currentDate) return`), a short `@summary` on `updateHeader` saying the header waits for the date, and a final newline in the spec.
